sentences.text: The largest known specimens of this ancient fish measure between 30 and 35 centimeters in length.
Its internal skeleton was composed of calcified cartilage, a tissue that hardens but remains flexible.
Large eyes positioned behind the nasal openings were supported by sclerotic rings, which are stiff rings made of calcified cartilage.
The mouth contained small, hook-shaped denticles that may have been composed of orthodentine, a type of dentine.
Males possessed a large, recurved denticle on their pelvic fin that functioned as a tenaculum, a specialized structure similar to those found in chimaeras.
Unlike modern chimaeras which have calcified rings, Iniopteryx lacked vertebral centra and had an entirely uncalcified notochord.
The animal was characterized by having fins similar to those of flying fish.
Researchers theorize that the low number of female fossils compared to males was caused by higher predation on females, while males used their denticle-covered pectoral fins for defense.
Fossil evidence from stomach infills shows that Iniopteryx ate arthropod exoskeletons, conodonts, and plant matter.
Fossils of Iniopteryx have been found in the U.S. states of Nebraska and Indiana.
However, fossils of Iniopteryx have been found abundantly only in Pennsylvania, North America.
The geological sites where Iniopteryx fossils were found are considered Konservat-Lagerstätten, meaning the fossils are exceptionally well preserved.
The large, nape-positioned pectoral fins were likely the primary means of locomotion for Iniopteryx.
Researchers compared the movement of Iniopteryx's pectoral fins to the flight stroke of a bird or the forelimbs of a sea turtle.
Researchers suggest that Iniopteryx had small, fragile teeth that limited its diet to soft food.
It is hypothesized that Iniopteryx and related iniopterygians were visitors to basin environments rather than permanent residents.
Iniopteryx is the type genus of the Iniopterygiformes, a group of cartilaginous fish debated as either stem-holocephalans or stem-group chondrichthyans related to Elasmobranchii and Holocephali.
Iniopteryx belongs to the order Iniopterygia.
Iniopteryx is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
The parent group of Iniopteryx is the family Iniopterygidae.
Iniopteryx is an extinct genus of holocephalans that appeared in the Carboniferous and disappeared by the end of the Permian.
Iniopteryx lived from the Moscovian to the Kasimovian stages, between 315.2 and 303.7 million years ago.
There are 14 recorded fossil occurrences of Iniopteryx in the Paleobiology Database.
It is debated whether Iniopteryx had a holostylic jaw suspension, as later research contradicted the original description that claimed the upper jaws were fused to the braincase.
